request.prompt: A creature sprite for RimWorld: the hell's lantern. A great, slow, segmented worm-thing the size of a muffalo, with a long, low, heavy serpentine body made of many successive transverse segment rings, its back and flanks studded with large swollen pods that glow a sickly orange in the dusk of the root-maze. The hell's lantern crawls through the Miasma at barely a walking pace, grazing, paying no attention to anything around it. Its mandibles carry a venom that leaves anything bitten sick and weakened. Visible features it must show: a great slow segmented worm the size of a muffalo; swollen pods studding its back and sides, glowing sickly orange; venomous mandibles at the front. Every view shows the same worm: a long, low, thick-bodied worm about three times as long as it is wide, built of many rounded transverse rings of the same girth along the middle, with the same large orange pods in a row along the back at the same size and count. The side view shows the full length of the body in profile: a rounded head with mandibles at the front, then a long run of transverse segment rings crossing the body from back to belly, pods along the spine and upper flank, and a body that tapers to a blunt rounded tail end at the rear. The rear view, seen from behind, shows the same ring-segmented body from the tail end: a blunt rounded terminal segment, concentric transverse rings receding toward the head, narrower than the body is long, with the orange pods on top of the back, the head and mandibles hidden behind the body. Realistic painterly vanilla RimWorld sprite style, clean dark outline, soft painted edges in a deeper shade of the local colour. Exactly ONE creature, centred, the whole body visible with nothing cut off. Fully transparent background with the creature alone on it.

request.prompt: A creature sprite for RimWorld: the runyip. A squat forest herbivore from Yavin 4 with branching antlers and a flexible snout. Dark brown stripes cross its pale coat, and its front toes bear claws. Visible features it must show: a squat, low-slung, broad barrel-bodied build on short legs. The shoulders carry a rounded hump that is the highest point of the back, and the topline slopes down from the shoulder hump to a lower, rounded rump. The head hangs low in front of the hump on a short neck, so the downturned snout tip nearly reaches the ground. The snout is a shorter, thicker tapir-like proboscis, a broad flexible downturned pig/tapir snout in a pale muzzle with natural skin folds and a clearly defined, heavy thick lower lip beneath it. Branching antler rack of one fixed size and shape, with the same span and height in every view. Clawed toes on the front feet instead of hooves. Pale coat crossed by bold dark brown stripes, the same stripe pattern in every view. Side view shows the profile with the shoulder hump as the highest point of the back, the rump lower, and the low-hung head. Front view shows the face with the broad pale snout and heavy lower lip, eyes toward the viewer, with the full antler rack and a wide chest. Rear view, seen from behind, shows the broad, heavy, barrel-shaped rump and haunches as wide as the front view's body, the shoulder hump rising above it, the tail toward the viewer, the eyes hidden, and the antler rack at the same width and height as in the front view. One consistent body across all views: the same bulk, the same width and the same antlers. Realistic painterly vanilla RimWorld sprite style, clean dark outline, soft painted edges in a deeper shade of the local colour. Exactly ONE creature, centred, the whole body visible with nothing cut off. Fully transparent background: no ground, no water, no shadow, no text, no border.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale. Each shows a squat, armoured, four-legged reptile under a large rosette of pointed grey-green and ochre leaves with orange-red blotches and yellow centres. Three dark-red stalks rise from the rosette, each ending in a ribbed, toothed jaw. Heights look alike across facings. The rosette spreads wider than the body in all three.
observed.south.png: Front view. A broad, blunt reptile head with two eyes and nostrils looks at the camera, tucked under the leaves. A heart-shaped leaf tip hangs over the brow. Two thick scaled forelegs with large pale claws splay out on either side, and a plated chest shows below the chin. Three trap stalks rise symmetrically above the rosette. Clean alpha.
observed.east.png: True side profile facing right. A long, low body with a jagged shell skirt sits under the rosette. A wedge-shaped, lizard-like head with a visible eye pokes out at the right on a short neck. Four clawed legs show, with no distinct tail. The three stalks are staggered along the body. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view. No face or eyes. A ribbed shell skirt with a zigzag lower edge shows beneath the leaves, with two scaled hind legs and claws and a dark underbelly between them. There is no visible tail. A small rounded dome pokes up behind the stalks above the leaves, reading as the top of the shell or head. Three stalks rise above. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: Beside the vanilla human the creature is about as tall as the pawn including stalks, and about one cell wide at max zoom. At 32 px per cell it reads as a spiky orange-green rosette with dark stalks on a dark low body. The trap heads shrink to small red blobs and the head is barely separable.
